dct_creator_sm: Government of the Northwest Territories, Environment and Climate Change.
dct_description_sm:
The Lockhart river watershed has been identified as one of the most important and pristine river systems in the Canadian Central Arctic. Development pressures within its watersheds currently include diamond mining and ongoing base metal exploration, as well as winter and all season road development, and recreational use. Potential cumulative effects of these developments require ongoing monitoring and assessment of the watershed’s water chemistry and water quantity. Both Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and the Department of Environment and Climate Change, GNWT has been collecting water chemistry and quantity (flow) data within this watershed since as early as 1969. Monitoring has increased both spatially and seasonally since the Snap Lake diamond mine opened in 2008 within this basin. This dataset includes water quality monitoring data collected since 2000.  Active water quality sampling has been carried out at 6 sites throughout the basin.  Water quality analysis is carried out for routine parameters including: physicals, solids, nutrients, ions, metals (including mercury), and chlorophyl A. Status and Trend reporting and monitoring program evaluation has been carried out approximate every 5 years.
